title: SweetCookie coverage shard
description: One shard of the feature ledger. Validated by ./gradlew specValidate. See spec/process.md and spec/constitution.md rule 9. A shard is a YAML array of entries; this schema describes the parsed JSON.

domain.description: Shard identifier. Must equal the file name without extension.

spec.description: The normative document that defines this domain's semantics.

upstream.description: Where the authoritative feature lists come from, so specUpstreamDiff can detect additions. A LIST, because one shard often draws on several places: block-components needs three, since Mojang documents components, trigger components and event responses as separate sections of one file. Null for domains with no machine-readable upstream source. A selector that resolves to no identifiers is a build failure, not an empty result - see spec/upstream/fetch.md.

source.description: Path within the pinned bedrock-samples snapshot. Never vendored; see spec/upstream/fetch.md.

nodePath.description: For doc_modules files, which are named `nodes[]` trees that an RFC 6901 pointer cannot address. Names the path to walk; the identifiers are the `name` of each child of the selected node. Example: ["Server Entity Documentation", "AI Goals"].

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer, for plain JSON. Mutually exclusive with nodePath.

idField.description: Field holding the identifier when the pointer targets an array of objects.

fqcn.description: Fully qualified Java class name, which must carry a matching @SpecImpl annotation.

conformanceRef.description: Path under spec/conformance/, without a trailing slash.

id.description: The Bedrock feature identifier, verbatim, including namespace. Immutable once merged.

status.description: See spec/normative/SC-000-conventions.md section 3. A human never writes 'implemented' — specReport promotes it when conformance passes.

impl.description: The implementing class. Required unless status is stub, unsupported or wontfix.

fields.description: Per-field fidelity. Keys are the Bedrock field names; values say what happens to each.

fidelity.description: An OBSERVABLE behavioural difference, not an implementation note. 'Not done yet' fails review; describe what a player would see. Required for partial, unsupported and wontfix. Optional for stub, whose meaning — recognised, parsed, no runtime effect — is already fully defined by the status.

conformance.description: Conformance cases proving this entry. Required for implemented and partial.

since.description: SweetCookie version in which this reached its current status.

bedrockSince.description: Bedrock format_version or engine version that introduced the feature, when known.

notes.description: Free text for anything that is not a fidelity statement — upstream documentation errors, links, observations.

diagnostics.description: Diagnostic codes this feature can emit.

entry.$comment: This schema governs SHAPE. The conditional rules that govern MEANING are enforced in code, by SpecValidateTask, and are deliberately NOT restated here: expressing them twice made every violation report twice, once in readable prose and once as an unreadable `allOf[2].then.not` path. SC-000 section 2 already draws this line - the schema governs shape, the prose governs meaning. The rules enforced in code are: implemented and partial must name an `impl` and at least one `conformance` case; partial, unsupported and wontfix must carry a `fidelity` note describing an observable difference; stub must not name an `impl`; and a (spec, id) pair must be unique across shards.
